problem: Native Word footer control ID -1419789921 was rejected by an unsigned content-control model, causing package-wide snapshot capture and unrelated Custom XML edits to fail. Word 2015 symEx runs were also removed by package/story MCE projections when carrying the required mc:Ignorable declaration, despite an existing typed symbol reader. Six UI-limited DOCX extension rows lacked native-parent operation coverage.
changes: Use signed i32 IDs consistently in content-control read models, authoring views/constructors, source snapshots, checksum reports and Custom XML binding reports. Parse the checked Int32 domain instead of rejecting native negative values; align with the existing signed block-identity API.

Keep the supported symEx namespace in Word-owned main-document, header/footer, note, comment, glossary and validation MCE profiles. Foreign namespaces remain distinct; no rendering capability is added.

Add ten native/native-parent regressions covering main/glossary stylesWithEffects lifecycle, cross-story checksum updates, formattingAllowed states and output quotas, checksum report distinctions, calendar MCE choices, inert web-link precedence, native signed IDs and main/secondary symbol projections.

Extend signed-boundary authoring/parser tests, correct the matrix description of detached Run symbol edits, and bind the new tests to scoped partial coverage. Historical fixture authoring records and the existing absence review for docx-097 remain unchanged.

api_behavior.signed_ids: ContentControl ID getters/constructors, AuthoringView, mutable writer controls, occurrence/snapshot IDs, ChecksumEntry::control_id and custom_xml::Binding::control_id now use i32/Option<i32>. Positive in-range IDs retain their values. Callers holding u32 IDs must use checked conversion before calling these constructors; IDs outside the signed range remain invalid on the wire.
api_behavior.source_identity: Missing and duplicate IDs remain separate source-order occurrences. IDs are not substituted for source-bound transaction identity. Native negative identifiers remain lexical source data rather than being clamped, dropped, reinterpreted as unsigned or normalized.
api_behavior.symbols: Known ignorable symEx content remains visible to typed readers. Raw Run replacement/clear is detached and leaves the containing package unchanged; there is no public package-level symEx transaction. Namespace admission does not implement shaping or glyph rendering.

verification_scope.signed_native_id: The unmodified word-tables-layout.docx footer2 control has ID -1419789921 and is now conformant without a repair diagnostic. Package-wide control capture and an unrelated Custom XML addition succeed while every original Word XML member stays exact. Minimum/maximum Int32 authoring and both out-of-range wire boundaries are covered.
verification_scope.effects_resources: Actual native style payloads supply 43/34 definitions for document/macro effects derivatives. Create, replacement, equal no-op, removal, exact-byte quota, missing-glossary refusal and stale replay are checked. Native glossary templates retain independent main/glossary effects resources. Unowned payloads, effective relationship/content-type graphs, ordinary styles, native text and macro data remain intact; file reopen/replay/inverse restore exact member payloads.
verification_scope.checksums: Explicit native-parent SDTs reference an added Custom XML item in the body and an existing header. Changing exact bytes <r/> to <r /> updates the two declared CRC/Base64 values AsOd4Q== to hS38mw== while retaining another checksum absence. Only those story owners and the store payload change; all XML outside the added controls and all other members remain exact. Malformed, missing-store, mismatch, absent and matching outcomes remain distinct; repair/missing-store refusal and inverse are checked.
verification_scope.formatting: Native DOCX/DOCM parents receive explicit lock derivatives. Absent, Allowed and Disallowed flags remain distinct through create/update/remove. Invalid lock combinations preserve earlier valid staging; stale patches and one-byte-under output budgets fail with typed errors. File reopen/inverse and unselected native text/macros remain exact.
verification_scope.calendar_and_web_links: Recognized MCE choices select Umalqura, while an unrecognized choice uses its Hijri fallback. Linked=true and Created=false are preserved, with Created(false) taking precedence. Both branches and unselected native XML survive exact save/reopen; no calendar computation or add-in activation occurs.
verification_scope.symbols: Explicit DOCX/DOCM symbol derivatives retain ordered symbols, absent versus explicit-empty/zero attributes and Unicode scalar validation through eager/source readers. Header, footnote, endnote, comment and glossary projections retain the supported symbols; source-backed note/comment readers agree. Foreign lookalikes remain unmodeled. Exact publication, save/reopen and untouched members are checked.
verification_scope.limits: The new extension payloads are library-authored derivatives of native parents. No native-app reopen, styles/effects rendering, calendar conversion, XPath/data-binding synchronization, external URI lookup, add-in/macro execution or formatting-UI enforcement is claimed. CRCs are advisory corruption checks, not authentication.

specification_evidence.finding: Word restricts ST_DecimalNumber to XML Schema int, which includes signed Int32 values. The actual native footer ID corroborates the signed model, already used by the raw block-identity API.
symEx extends a run and its namespace prefix must be declared ignorable for compatibility. An understood symbol namespace must therefore survive Word-owned MCE semantic projection.

specification_evidence.reference: [MS-DOCX] 2.11/2.13 and existing bounded checksum/formatting owner contracts
specification_evidence.source: Local specification and tracked public owner documentation/tests
specification_evidence.finding: Checksum bytes and formatting flags are metadata. The tests use established exact-byte CRC vectors and retain absent versus explicit state without implying authentication or Word UI enforcement.
